{{Quote|I think the Jedi are a massive system of unchecked power, posing as a religion, a delusional cult that claims to control the uncontrollable.|Worus Rayencourt|<ref name="TA">{{Acolyte|The Acolyte (episode)}}</ref>}}
'''Worus Rayencourt''' was a [[human]] who served as a [[senator]] of the [[Galactic Republic]]'s [[Galactic Senate|Senate]], representing the [[Thusa sector]] during the [[High Republic Era]]. Having [[Anti-Jedi sentiment|anti-Jedi views]], he believed the [[Jedi Order]] to be a danger and was working on getting an external review of the Order passed in [[132 BBY]]. That [[Standard year|year]], he discovered that [[Jedi Master]] [[Vernestra Rwoh]] was leading a [[Indara's murder|murder]] [[Mae's quest|investigation]] without reporting it to the Senate, prompting him to report this discovery to [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Veeth Drellik]] and confront Rwoh.

He was later a part of a Senate tribunal where Rwoh provided a report on the investigation. Rwoh lied to the tribunal, framing the [[Death|dead]] [[Jedi]] Master [[Sol]] as the killer to cover up the truth. Rayencourt used her report to argue for an external review of the Order to begin immediately, but Drellik ignored his request.

==Biography==
===Anti-Jedi campaign===
{{Quote|You project an image of goodness and restraint, but it's only a matter of time before one of you snaps. And when, not 'if,' that happens, who will be strong enough to stop him?|Rayencourt|<ref name="TA" />}}
[[File:Chuwant-TeachCorrupt.png|thumb|right|200px|Isedwa Chuwant updates Vernestra Rwoh on Worus Rayencourt's proposal.]]
Worus Rayencourt was a [[human]] [[senator]] of the [[Galactic Republic]] during the [[High Republic Era]], representing<ref name="AcolyteVG" /> the [[Mid Rim Territories|Mid Rim's]]<ref name="Appendix">{{GalaxyMapAppendix}}</ref> [[Thusa sector]] in the [[Galactic Senate]].<ref name="AcolyteVG" /> In [[132 BBY]],<ref name="Date">{{TheAcolyteDate}}</ref> he campaigned for an external review of the [[Jedi Order]] to pass in the Galactic Senate and received increased support from his fellow senators.<ref name="TC" /> The [[Mirialan]] [[Jedi Master]] [[Vernestra Rwoh]] and [[Abednedo]] senator [[Isedwa Chuwant]]<ref name="AcolyteVG" /> discussed Rayencourt's increasing popularity in the Senate and his proposal, with Chuwant informing<ref name="TC" /> her that his<ref name="AcolyteVG" /> fellow senators from the [[Expansion Region]] were going to vote in support of the review. While Rwoh worried that Rayencourt's [[anti-Jedi sentiment|anti-Jedi views]] swayed too many others, Chuwant assured the Jedi that the Order had a history of transparency with the Senate and there was no need to worry about the review.<ref name="TC" />

Later, Rayencourt heard of a [[Indara's murder|murder]] [[Mae's quest|investigation]] that the [[Jedi]] were conducting without a report to the Senate, prompting him to inform [[Supreme Chancellor]]<ref name="TA" /> [[Veeth Drellik]]<ref name="AcolyteVG" /> of the Jedi's lack of transparency<ref name="TA" /> and push for a Senate tribunal with Rwoh.<ref name="AcolyteVG" /> After his report to the Chancellor,<ref name="Databank" /> he immediately<ref name="Topps">{{Topps|set=2025 Topps Chrome Star Wars|cardname=Senator Ravencourt|link=https://www.ebay.com/itm/297586373080}}</ref> visited the<ref name="TA" /> [[Jedi Diplomatic Tower]] on<ref name="AcolyteVG" /> the [[Core Worlds]] [[planet]]<ref name="Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars Encyclopedia: The Comprehensive Guide to the Star Wars Galaxy]]''</ref> [[Coruscant]] to speak with Rwoh. [[Padawan]] [[Mog Adana]]<ref name="AcolyteVG" /> let Rayencourt into the [[control room]], where he waited for the Jedi Master. After she arrived to the room, she inquired about the reason for Rayencourt's<ref name="TA" /> unwelcome<ref name="Explained">{{SW|url=news/the-acolyte-highlights-the-acolyte|text=''The Acolyte'' Explained | Highlights from "The Acolyte"}}</ref> visit.<ref name="TA" />

[[File:TenseMeeting-TheAcolyte.png|thumb|left|300px|Rayencourt confronted Rwoh on his distrust of the Jedi Order.]]
Rayencourt mentioned that he had heard about the Order's investigation, and the pair briefly discussed it, with Rwoh attempting to end the conversation by thanking him for his concern and trying to leave the room. The senator stopped her by saying that despite her personal opinion, the external review was not a personal vendetta against the Jedi Order. He went on to explain that he viewed the Jedi as a delusional [[Religion|cult]] wielding unchecked power, making potential [[Dark Jedi|rogue]] Jedi dangerous. Before leaving the control room he also told Rwoh that he had informed Drellik of the lack of transparency surrounding the murder investigation, advising her to arrest the murder suspect by the time Drellik summoned her for a Senate tribunal.<ref name="TA" />

===Senate tribunal===
{{Quote|Sixteen years ago, four Jedi were stationed on the planet Brendok. There they discovered a Force cult of witches. A conflict ensued. There were many casualties. Afterwards, the Jedi conspired to keep their actions secret. Recently, when the truth threatened to come out, a rogue Jedi named Sol killed his accomplices to maintain the cover story. Speaking on behalf of the High Council, we wholly condemn the actions of Master Sol.|Vernestra Rwoh, deceiving a Senate tribunal|<ref name="TA" />}}
[[File:VernestraSenateTribunal-TheAcolyte.png|thumb|right|300px|Vernestra Rwoh deceived the Senate tribunal about the truth behind the murders.]]
Rayencourt was one of the senators present for the tribunal he warned Rwoh about. Rwoh reported that, [[148 BBY|sixteen years]] earlier, a [[Brendok four|quartet]] of Jedi participated in a [[Mission to Brendok|mission]] to<ref name="TA" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories]] planet<ref name="AcolyteVG" /> [[Brendok]], where their actions led to the destruction of a [[the Force|Force]] [[Brendok coven|cult]] of [[witch]]es. She deceived the tribunal by saying that the Jedi Master [[Sol]] went rogue when truth about the events threatened to be revealed and hunted down the other three Jedi involved,<ref name="TA" /> when in truth the killers were the [[Force-sensitive]] [[assassin]] [[Mae-ho Aniseya|Mae Aniseya]] and her [[The Stranger|nameless]] [[Sith Master]].<ref name="AcolyteVG" />

Rayencourt and Drellik shared a look when Rwoh mentioned Sol's alleged murder of his compatriots. While Rwoh condemned Sol's actions on behalf of the [[Jedi High Council]], Rayencourt suggested to the [[Tarsunt]] Chancellor that an external review of the Order must begin immediately. Drellik did not react to the senator's proposal, instead further discussing the rogue Jedi with Rwoh.<ref name="TA" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|The majority of my colleagues can't imagine a galaxy without the Jedi. And I can understand why. When you're looking up to heroes, you don't have to face what's right in front of you.|Rayencourt|<ref name="TA" />}}
[[File:Rayencourt-TheAcolyte.png|thumb|left|190px|Worus Rayencourt campaigned for increased supervision of the Jedi Order to improve safety.]]
Worus Rayencourt was a [[Color|dark]]-skinned human with brown eyes and black hair who had a height of 1.78 [[meter]]s. He was a suspicious representative<ref name="Databank" /> who advocated for stricter supervision of the Jedi Order.<ref name="AcolyteVG" /> Rayencourt had a strong dislike for the Order,<ref name="TA" /> questioning their nobility<ref name="Databank" /> and considering them a delusional cult that possessed unchecked power. He perceived his fellow senators' positive opinion of the Jedi to be caused by hero worship. While Rayencourt disliked the Order, he insisted that his attempts for an external review were not motivated by a personal vendetta.<ref name="TA" /> While Senator Isedwa Chuwant thought of Rayencourt as an ambitious politician trying to secure power for himself,<ref name="TC" /> Rayencourt insisted that his concerns were merely about safety. One of his doubts was that anyone would be able to stop a Jedi who failed to keep their emotions in check, which he expressed to Vernestra Rwoh and considered impossible.<ref name="TA" />

Rwoh, meanwhile, believed that Rayencourt's distaste of the Jedi Order was rooted in fear.<ref name="TC" /> When discovering that Rwoh kept a Jedi investigation secret from the Senate, he confronted her about her actions and also alerted the Chancellor of them. Despite Rayencourt's anti-Jedi sentiments, he was familiar with the Order's saying "[[May the Force be with you]]" and was aware that Rwoh got nauseous in [[hyperspace]]; however, he incorrectly believed the problem to be her stomach, when in fact it was her head.<ref name="TA" />

==Equipment==
During his conversation with Vernestra Rwoh, Rayencourt wore [[clothing]] composed of multiple layers, including wine-red [[robe]]s that were partially covered by a cream-colored layer with a black and gold hexagon pattern. Parts of the latter layer were connected with strings of white-gold beads, and the outfit also featured shoes and a [[necklace]] with a large pendant. Rayencourt later wore a similar outfit to the Senate tribunal, changing the uppermost layer for one with a hexagon pattern that was red and gold.<ref name="TA" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Welcome to the world of politics.|Worus Rayencourt, to Vernestra Rwoh, in a deleted scene from "The Acolyte"|<ref name="Art of Acolyte">''[[The Art of Star Wars: The Acolyte]]''</ref>}}
[[File:TheAcolyteVisualGuide.jpg|thumb|right|200px|''Star Wars: The Acolyte: The Visual Guide'' marked the first use of the senator's first name of Worus.]]
Worus Rayencourt was first mentioned in "[[Teach / Corrupt]],"<ref name="TC" /> the sixth episode of the live-action [[Disney+]] series [[Star Wars: The Acolyte|''The Acolyte'']], which released on [[July 2]], [[2024]].<ref name="Insider">{{InsiderCite|229|Star Wars: The Acolyte Companion|''Star Wars: The Acolyte'' Companion}}</ref> The senator made his first appearance in "[[The Acolyte (episode)|The Acolyte]],"<ref name="TA" /> the eighth episode of the series, released on [[July 16]] of the same year.<ref name="Insider" /> In the episode, he was portrayed by [[David Harewood]],<ref name="TA" /> and the scene in which Rayencourt met with Rwoh was filmed at [[Shinfield Studios]],<ref name="Fantha Part II">{{WebCite|url=https://www.fanthatracks.com/news/the-acolyte-a-journey-to-the-filming-locations-part-2-uk|text=The Acolyte: A journey to the filming locations Part 2: UK|archivedate=20250516041344}}</ref> [[Wikipedia:England|England]].<ref name="Julian Foddy">{{Lucasfilm|url=news/julian-foddy-acolyte|text=''The Acolyte'' Visual Effects Supervisor Julian Foddy}}</ref>

The individual's first name of Worus was introduced in the [[2025]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: The Acolyte: The Visual Guide]]'' written by [[Pablo Hidalgo]].<ref name="AcolyteVG" /> Rayencourt was featured in a scene that was scripted and shot,<ref name="Art of Acolyte" /> though ultimately cut from the series final episode.<ref name="TA" /> In the scene, as Vernestra Rwoh was leaving the Senate hearing, the senator would have welcomed her to the world of politics.<ref name="Art of Acolyte" />
